<prediction>The EBM model predicted 73.1 bikes rented for this hour, while 63 were actually counted. The model overshoots by about 10 bikes, which is a moderate match — reasonable in direction but not perfectly precise for a quiet late-night Saturday in March.</prediction>

<drivers>The single strongest damping factor is the year: yr=0 (2011) carries the longest blue bar, pulling the prediction down most forcefully. The model recognises 2011 as the lower-demand phase of the system's history. Closely behind it, the interaction between month and year adds a second blue bar — March 2011 together reinforces the seasonal and yearly weakness, compounding the year effect. Third in rank is temperature: at about 14.8 °C the evening is still fairly cool for cycling, and this blue bar reflects that cooler temperatures dampen demand noticeably. On the positive side, the combination of the late-night hour (22:00) on a Saturday pushes back with the strongest red bar — Saturday nights tend to attract leisure riders even late into the evening — supported by smaller upward contributions from the hour itself and the clear weather conditions.</drivers>

<recommendation>For late Saturday nights in early 2011-like low-demand periods, it may be worth slightly reducing the number of bikes pre-positioned at busy leisure stations compared to warmer months, as cool March temperatures and the early-year growth phase together suppress overall ridership. Maintenance or rebalancing runs could be scheduled around this late-night window when actual rental volumes remain modest despite the Saturday leisure effect.</recommendation>
